  
**LLM PROMPT**

Ring Camera interface 

Give the full technical implementation details for: 

We have Ring security camera installed in our office. User Ring Developer tools, build a web application and mobile application to connect to ring cameras and stream the videos and perform other operations (configuration, replay etc.) 

Once the video is captured, analyze the videos (using computer vision techniques) to count the people in the room and do face recognition. 

Create a technical specification as well.

\------------------------- CHATGPT \------------------------

Yes. This is technically feasible, but I would design it as a **Ring-integrated video intelligence platform**, rather than trying to replace the Ring infrastructure itself.

Ring's current developer platform explicitly supports third-party applications accessing **live video, motion events, device status, event history and video data**, and its developer documentation specifically describes using Ring video streams as input to your own computer-vision/AI pipeline. ([Ring Developer](https://developer.ring.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

There is one important distinction: **Ring API capabilities are permission/device/subscription dependent**, so configuration/replay/download capabilities should be implemented only against the exact APIs exposed to your approved Ring developer application. Don't build against unofficial/private Ring APIs.

**7\. Live video architecture**  
For live viewing:  
Browser  
   │  
   │ HTTPS  
   ▼  
FastAPI  
   │  
   │ create stream session  
   ▼  
Ring WHEP  
   │  
   │ WebRTC  
   ▼  
Browser  
Ring's published developer example creates an RTCPeerConnection, establishes a video-only receiver and sends the SDP offer to the WHEP streaming endpoint. ([Ring Developer](https://developer.ring.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
Your React application should therefore have:  
CameraPlayer.tsx

CameraGrid.tsx

LiveView.tsx

StreamManager.ts

WebRTCManager.ts  
A simplified browser flow:  
const pc \= new RTCPeerConnection({  
    iceServers: \[...\]  
});

pc.addTransceiver("video", {  
    direction: "recvonly"  
});

pc.ontrack \= event \=\> {  
    videoElement.srcObject \=  
        event.streams\[0\] ||  
        new MediaStream(\[event.track\]);  
};

const offer \= await pc.createOffer();

await pc.setLocalDescription(offer);

// send SDP to backend/Ring WHEP endpoint  
The exact endpoint and authentication mechanism should come from the current Ring developer documentation associated with your approved application rather than hard-coding an unofficial endpoint.

**10\. People counting**  
There are actually **three different metrics** you should support.  
**A. Current people count**  
Number of people currently visible  
**B. Entry/exit count**  
Person crosses virtual line  
          ↓  
        ENTER  
**C. Occupancy**  
Current occupancy \=  
entries \- exits  
These should not be confused.

**11\. People detection**  
Recommended model:  
YOLO  
or  
RT-DETR  
Output:  
{  
  "class": "person",  
  "confidence": 0.94,  
  "bbox": \[  
    421,  
    120,  
    612,  
    580  
  \]  
}  
Then tracking:  
Detection  
    ↓  
ByteTrack  
    ↓  
Track ID  
Example:  
Person A → track\_id 102  
Person B → track\_id 103  
Person C → track\_id 104  
This prevents counting the same person repeatedly.

**12\. Virtual line counting**  
For an office entrance:  
              OFFICE  
──────────────────────────  
        ↑  
        │  
        │ EXIT  
────────┼─────────────────  
        │  
        │ ENTER  
        ↓  
              LOBBY  
Define:  
line \= \[(x1,y1),(x2,y2)\]  
When the tracked person's trajectory crosses the line:  
if crossed\_line(previous\_position,  
                current\_position,  
                counting\_line):

    if direction \== "IN":  
        entries \+= 1

    elif direction \== "OUT":  
        exits \+= 1

**15\. Face database**  
Never store only photographs.  
Store:  
person  
 ├── person\_id  
 ├── employee\_id  
 ├── name  
 ├── department  
 ├── status  
 └── consent\_status

face\_template  
 ├── template\_id  
 ├── person\_id  
 ├── embedding  
 ├── model\_version  
 ├── created\_at  
 └── revoked\_at

PostgreSQL:  
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

CREATE TABLE face\_templates (  
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,  
    person\_id UUID NOT NULL,  
    embedding vector(512),  
    model\_version VARCHAR(50),  
    created\_at TIMESTAMP,  
    revoked\_at TIMESTAMP  
);  
Search:  
SELECT  
    person\_id,  
    1 \- (embedding \<=\> :query\_embedding) AS similarity  
FROM face\_templates  
WHERE revoked\_at IS NULL  
ORDER BY embedding \<=\> :query\_embedding  
LIMIT 5;  
Then apply a recognition threshold.  
**Do not use a generic threshold blindly.** Calibrate it using your actual camera, lighting, camera angle and population.

**16\. Unknown-person detection**  
The system should not simply say:  
Face \= John  
Instead:  
Face  
 │  
 ▼  
Embedding  
 │  
 ▼  
Nearest Known Face  
 │  
 ▼  
Similarity  
 │  
 ├── \> threshold → John  
 │  
 └── \< threshold → UNKNOWN  
Example:  
{  
  "identity": "UNKNOWN",  
  "confidence": 0.32  
}  
This is much safer than forcing every face into an identity.

**17\. Face recognition should be optional**  
I would actually make the product modes configurable:  
**Mode 1 — Anonymous analytics**  
People \= 23  
No identity.  
**Mode 2 — Person detection**  
Person detected  
**Mode 3 — Face detection**  
Face detected  
**Mode 4 — Authorized face recognition**  
John  
Employee \#102

This separation is important for privacy and compliance.  
India's DPDP framework treats identifiable digital information as personal data and emphasizes lawful processing, purpose limitation, data minimization, security and deletion. ([Indian Kanoon](https://indiankanoon.org/doc/3510545/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
India's government has also previously described facial-pattern biometrics as biometric information under the earlier sensitive-personal-data framework. ([Press Information Bureau](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1885963&lang=2&reg=48&utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
Therefore, for an office deployment, **do not silently build a system that identifies employees from CCTV footage**. Establish the lawful basis, notice/consent and retention/access policies with your legal/privacy team before enabling recognition.

**18\. Privacy architecture**  
I recommend:  
Camera  
   ↓  
Video  
   ↓  
AI Processing  
   ↓  
Anonymous metadata  
rather than storing all video indefinitely.  
For example:  
Raw video  
     ↓  
AI processing  
     ↓  
Events \+ metrics  
     ↓  
Raw video deleted after X days  
Face templates:  
Employee leaves company  
        ↓  
Identity revoked  
        ↓  
Face template deleted  
You should implement:  
Retention Policy  
Consent/Notice  
Data Subject Requests  
Deletion  
Audit Trail  
Role Based Access  
Encryption  
Access Logs

**36\. Configuration engine**  
Create:

Retention Configuration  
Example:  
{

    "face\_recognition": false,  
    "people\_counting": true  
  }  
}  
Ring configuration itself should be treated separately because the set of remotely controllable Ring settings depends on the supported developer APIs/device capabilities.

**37\. Ring capability abstraction**  
This is very important.  
Don't write:  
ring.camera.set\_everything(...)  
Instead:  
class RingCameraAdapter:

    async def get\_cameras():  
        ...

    async def get\_status():  
        ...

    async def start\_live\_view():  
        ...

    async def get\_events():  
        ...

    async def get\_recording():  
        ...

    async def get\_capabilities():  
        ...

    async def update\_configuration():  
        ...  
Then:  
Ring API  
    ↓  
RingAdapter  
    ↓  
Your normalized camera model  
This protects your application against Ring API changes.

TLS

**Face data**  
Encryption at rest  
Encryption in transit  
Strict RBAC  
Separate access policy  
Audit logging  
Deletion workflow  
Ring itself states that its video is protected using encryption mechanisms including AES, TLS and SRTP. ([Ring](https://ring.com/privacy?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**41\. Natural-language video search**  
This could become a particularly strong product feature.  
User asks:  
"Show me everyone who entered the office between 8:00 and 9:00."  
System:  
NL Query  
 ↓  
Query Parser  
 ↓  
Camera/Event DB  
 ↓  
Vector/metadata search  
 ↓  
Relevant video segments  
 ↓  
Timeline  
Or:  
"Who entered the server room after 8 PM yesterday?"  
Result:  
22:14 — Unknown  
22:36 — John

Clicking the result opens the corresponding video segment.

**43\. Important Ring-specific constraint**  
Ring's current developer ecosystem is substantially better positioned for this than the old unofficial integrations: Ring explicitly advertises third-party applications using live video, motion events, device status and event history, and specifically identifies computer-vision and video-intelligence applications as supported use cases. ([Ring Developer](https://developer.ring.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
However, **do not assume that every operation available in the Ring consumer application is exposed through the developer API**. For example, "replay", download, camera configuration, audio/talk, continuous recording and other functions should be treated as separate capabilities and validated against the exact API scopes and camera model you obtain during developer onboarding.  
Ring also states that third-party app access requires explicit authorization and lets users choose which Ring devices are shared with an application. ([Ring](https://co.ring.com/support/articles/2be4d/Understanding-how-third-party-developer-apps-use-your-data?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
For continuous recording, Ring currently supports it only on eligible devices/plans and says 24/7 recordings are temporarily stored in the cloud for up to 14 days. ([Ring Partners](https://partners.ring.com/support/articles/ujb81/continuous-live-view?hasLangChanged=true&utm_source=chatgpt.com))

**46\. My recommendation for your office**  
For the **first implementation**, I would build this exact flow:  
                    RING CAMERA  
                         │  
                         ▼  
                  RING DEVELOPER  
                         │  
             ┌───────────┴───────────┐  
             │                       │  
         Live Video              Motion Event  
             │                       │  
             ▼                       ▼  
       WebRTC/WHEP              Webhook API  
             │                       │  
             └───────────┬───────────┘  
                         ▼  
                   XCEL BACKEND  
                         │  
                ┌────────┴────────┐  
                │                 │  
                ▼                 ▼  
           Live Viewer        AI Pipeline  
                                  │  
                    ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐  
                    │             │             │  
                    ▼             ▼             ▼  
                 Person        Tracking        Face  
                Detection                     Recognition  
                    │             │             │  
                    └─────────────┼─────────────┘  
                                  ▼  
                           ANALYTICS ENGINE  
                                  │  
                    ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐  
                    ▼             ▼             ▼  
                Occupancy       Alerts       Reports  
                    │  
                    ▼  
              PostgreSQL  
              \+ pgvector

This gives you a **working Ring integration first**, while making the AI layer independent enough that you can later connect any ONVIF/RTSP/IP camera.

**One caution on face recognition:** because this is an office environment, I would make face recognition a separately gated enterprise feature, with explicit privacy notice, defined purpose, access controls, retention/deletion and appropriate legal review. The DPDP Act framework is especially relevant because facial identification creates identifiable digital personal data and the Act establishes requirements around lawful processing, notice, consent where applicable, minimization and security. ([India Code](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/22037/1/a2023-22.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

[Ring Developer Platform](https://developer.ring.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) — this should be the starting point for registering the application, obtaining the current API documentation/scopes and testing against your actual Ring camera.  
If this is intended as an **XCEL commercial product**, the next logical step is to turn this into a formal **Software Technical Specification (STS)** with component-level APIs, PostgreSQL schema, Kafka event schemas, Ring OAuth sequence diagrams, WebRTC implementation, AI inference pipeline, React screens, React Native screens, AWS infrastructure and a phased development plan.
